c0622: Choose your legal structure: LLC vs S corp
c0625: The financial plan assumes an effective income tax rate of 25% (21% federal plus state), as for a C corporation. An LLC taxed as a pass-through pays through your personal return instead, and early losses carry forward as net operating losses. Compare an LLC vs S corp election with your CPA, using the plan's numbers.
c0626: Form the LLC with your state and get the EIN
c0629: Filing fees, annual reports and franchise taxes vary by state. Check your Secretary of State's website before you file.
c0633: State payroll and unemployment registration (and workers' comp insurance)
c0634: Premiums depend on your state, your payroll and your job classes. Get quotes from your insurance broker or the state fund.
c0635: Apply for the beer & wine license (state + local)
c0636: Start in week 1: ask your state alcohol beverage control (ABC) agency and your city what they need, and file as soon as you sign the lease: state and local approval can take months, and costs and timelines vary widely. Never open counting on it, and add liquor liability to your insurance.
c0637: Business bank account and business card
c0638: Keep them separate from personal accounts: card terminal settlements, delivery marketplace payouts and supplier payments all run through them.
c0639: Accountant / bookkeeper and a POS that reports sales tax
c0641: Payroll and onboarding for your team. Pick a POS that calculates and reports sales tax by jurisdiction before you buy it, and ask your CPA how often your state wants sales tax returns.
c0642: Take the plan to two SBA 7(a) lenders and compare loan offers
c0644: General liability, liquor liability, property and workers' comp insurance
c0656: Check the electrical service and the gas capacity
c0660: Confirm the hood and duct route to the roof with your mechanical contractor
c0663: Negotiate the lease: free-rent period during build-out and security deposit
c0669: Commission architect and MEP drawings, including the hood and duct
c0673: Zoning approval and certificate of occupancy
c0676: Building permit for the build-out and the hood
c0678: The build-out and the hood run through their own building permit and inspections: ask the building department which drawings and sign-offs they require.
c0699: The final sign-offs (electrical, gas, mechanical, fire and building) and the certificate of occupancy. Keep them together with the gas paperwork: your health department and your insurer may ask for them.
c0711: Submit your plans for health department plan review, apply for the health permit and book the pre-opening inspection
c0734: Traceability and records: lots, temperatures and suppliers
c0739: Allergens on delivery marketplaces and on your website
c0742: Temperature of orders leaving the shop
c0747: Set pay rates against the state and local minimum wage and post the labor law posters
c0750: Offer letters for full-time and part-time staff
c0751: With schedule, pay rate and role. Collect a W-4 and an I-9 (with identity documents) from every hire, the I-9 within 3 business days of the start date. Classify people correctly: a 1099 contractor who works your schedule at your address is a misclassification risk.
c0756: Keep hours for every employee, part-time included (FLSA recordkeeping). A time clock in the POS makes it simple; agree with your CPA how to store the records.
c0760: Own delivery drivers: W-2 employees only
c0762: Your own drivers are employees on payroll (W-2), and because they drive their own cars on your behalf you also need hired and non-owned auto insurance (check your state). Do not treat them as independent contractors. Drivers for DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub work for the marketplace, not for you.
c0763: Food handler cards and a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
c0767: OSHA basics: safety plan and training
c0770: Employee health policy and first aid
c0772: Have every new hire sign an employee health agreement (report illness symptoms; Food Code 2-201) and stock a first aid kit.
c0773: Allergen information on the menu or by staff script, with a written record
c0774: In writing on the menu or, if staff give it verbally, backed by a written record kept on site and a sign telling guests to ask. Keep one allergen matrix up to date for the whole menu.
c0790: Utensils and napkins on request for to-go orders
c0791: Hand out utensils and napkins only when guests ask for them, and keep the to-go containers in stock; check your city's packaging rules.
c0792: Local packaging ordinances: fees and bans
c0802: Sign up with the delivery marketplaces (DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub)
c0806: Run a trademark search first to make sure the name is not registered in your class (restaurant services), and check your state's business name registry.
c0815: Open in January, Month 1 of the plan
c0817: The plan starts in January and the ramp-up falls on the slowest months, January and February: that is why working capital matters. If you open in another month, rotate the seasonality row of the "12-Month Cash Flow" tab.
c0824: Check temperatures and records on day one
c0827: Health inspection: written food safety plan and records at hand
c0843: Review the delivery marketplace statement each month
c0846: Compare actual sales and costs with the plan each month
c0848: Track cash flow month by month and the minimum balance
c0849: January and February are the slowest months and coincide with the launch: look at the balance of each month before a big payment.
